thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO alert: canary cluster 'canary-east-3' p99 latency breached 1.5s for 5m. auto-pager triggered. Route: /v1/generate (streaming).
Rae (oncall): acked — looking. tagging Nate to dig into serving side. @Nate H can you take lead?
Nate H: on it. quick glance at console shows a spike starting at 4832109400, coincident with a canary traffic shift (10% -> 40%). rolling rollout started ~4832109300.
Priya K: adding context — rollout pushed new tokenizer+kv patch (model v13b-q4 -> v13b-q4a). It changed tokenization heuristics (word-splitting) which may increase sequence lengths for some queries.
Maya S: got a customer ping saying streaming responses stall at ~8-12s then time out. customer_id=acme-inc. they see partial chunks then nothing.
Leo T: grabbing metrics: p50 120ms, p95 420ms, p99 1.8s. streaming chunk interval median increased from 200ms to 1.2s for canary nodes.
Nate H: I can repro locally with a short prompt that used to be 120 tokens, now tokenized to 220 tokens because of tokenizer change. That doubles KV cache warmup overhead.
Priya K: Notes: the new tokenizer merges some emojis into multi-token sequences; also we changed prefix caching key format slightly in runtime which may cause cache misses when model variant changes. possible double-cause: longer seqs + cold kvcache.
Rae (oncall): customer impact? Maya?
Maya S: acme-inc saw 37 distinct failed streams in the last 6m, they flagged 5% of requests errored with client-side timeout. Noted increased not-ready stream reattachments.
incident-bot: pager escalation: severity=page, slack-channel=pager-duty, runbook=streaming-tail.
Nate H: quick plan: 1) throttle canary traffic back to 10% 2) enable fallback to previous tokenizer/model variant for streaming endpoints 3) gather full pcap/logs for affected nodes. Can someone execute throttle?
Priya K: I can flip traffic routing. Running command:```sh
redwood-route set-weight canary-east-3 --route /v1/generate --weight 10
```
Priya K: done. confirmed canary weight back to 10% (propagating).
Leo T: after throttle p99 dropped to 900ms within 40s, streaming chunk interval back to ~230ms for majority of flows. Still surface tailers at ~1.1s.
Rae (oncall): good. We're reducing blast radius. Next: rollback vs hotfix? Which is faster?
Nate H: rollback model variant for streaming is simplest and fastest. We have v13b-q4 snapshot pinned as previous.
Priya K: issuing rollback for streaming route only:```sh
redwood-model promote --cluster canary-east-3 --route /v1/generate --model v13b-q4 --scope streaming
```
Priya K: promoted. watch logs.
incident-bot: deploy-bot: streaming rollback initiated by Priya K at 4832110001.
Leo T: observing streaming sessions — error rate dropped to baseline within 90s. aknowledging acme-inc reduced errors to 1 in last 5m.
Maya S: notified acme-inc that we rolled back their streaming path and are monitoring; they replied :thumbsup: and asked for postmortem.
Nate H: root cause draft: tokenizer change increased token counts for certain inputs -> more KV cache warmups and increased per-token kernel switching due to unexpected sequence-length distribution -> canary nodes missed warm cache and showed tail stalls for streaming chunk emissions. Also a concurrent small change in cache key encoding prevented some prefix reuse across node reboot during rollout.
Rae (oncall): action items: - Nate to produce perf repro and verify fix (hotfix tokenizer or kv key compatibility) - Priya to coordinate canary rollout gating and add preflight that checks token distribution delta - Leo to add streaming-chunk interval SLO (alert if median chunk interval > 500ms for 2m) - Maya to draft customer-facing incident note for acme-inc and any others flagged
Nate H: starting repro harness now. I already have a failing test:```python
# repro harness snippet
resp = client.stream("I'm trying to get a long code block with emojis 😂🤯 and it suddenly stalls...")
for chunk in resp:
    print(chunk.timestamp, len(chunk.tokens))
```
Nate H: initial hypothesis for hotfix: revert tokenizer tweak for emojis OR add token-length normalization on inference path to avoid doubling KV warm-ups. We'll bench both.
Priya K: We'll also add a canary gating check that compares token length histograms across cohorts and rejects rollout if p99 tokens increase > 30% vs baseline. I'll raise PR.
Leo T: logging note: we saw `mux:stream_write_timeout` in node logs around 4832109456 — adding that pattern to incident alerts.
incident-bot: document-link: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/4832109999 (auto-created).
Rae (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline in 40m; Nate, please own postmortem and tie any churn to release process. Priya, keep rollout paused until we have gating. Maya, escalate to CSM for acme follow-up.
Maya S: will draft CSM note and include timeline & rollback details.
Nate H: will produce perf numbers and patch candidate by EOD UTC. Will include microbench results and a reproducer dataset.
Priya K: opened PR #5127 with gating check and reverted tokenizer change for streaming-config; test job queued.
Leo T: adding temporary alert silence for canary noise now that we've throttled. Will keep watch.
Rae (oncall): thanks all. closing page once postmortem skeleton exists. Please update thread with links to PR and postmortem doc.
Maya S: noted — sending acme follow-up now.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: page resolved at 4832110300 (conditions returned to normal).
